hints.title: Core Idea
hints.text: Calculate the total active running duration across all server sessions and convert the aggregated seconds into full days.

hints.title: Session Pairing
hints.text: Use window lead partitioned by server identifier ordered by status time to match each start timestamp with its corresponding stop timestamp.

hints.title: Aggregation Formula
hints.text: Sum the timestamp differences in seconds for rows with start status, divide by eighty-six thousand four hundred, and floor the outcome.

hints.title: Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH ServerNeighbors AS (
    SELECT 
        status_time, 
        session_status, 
        LEAD(status_time) OVER (
            PARTITION BY server_id 
            ORDER BY status_time
        ) AS next_status_time 
    FROM Servers
) 
SELECT 
    FLOOR(SUM(TIMESTAMPDIFF(SECOND, status_time, next_status_time)) / 86400) AS total_uptime_days 
FROM ServerNeighbors 
WHERE session_status = 'start';
```

variables: N: total log records in Servers table
complexity.notes: Partition sorting by server followed by single aggregation pass.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Self joins without window indexing lead to quadratic comparison times.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use window lead to seamlessly pair start and stop log events.

WITH ServerNeighbors AS (
    SELECT 
        status_time, 
        session_status, 
        LEAD(status_time) OVER (
            PARTITION BY server_id 
            ORDER BY status_time
        ) AS next_status_time 
    FROM Servers
) 
SELECT 
    FLOOR(SUM(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (next_status_time - status_time))) / 86400) AS total_uptime_days 
FROM ServerNeighbors 
WHERE session_status = 'start';
